summary.text: The continental slope is the part of a continental margin that begins at the shelf break, where the generally flat shelf ends and the angle increases drastically.
It can stand 1–5 km above the deep-ocean floor and often has submarine canyons cut into it.
At its base the angle suddenly decreases and the seafloor levels out into the continental rise.

facts.label: Part of
facts.value: One of three parts of the continental margin

items.prompt: A submersible glides out over the shallow seabed off a coast. What tells the pilot it has just passed onto the continental slope?

options.label: The seafloor suddenly tilts much more steeply
The seabed rises up toward the surface

items.explain: The flat shelf ends at the shelf break, where the angle increases drastically, and the slope begins there.

items.prompt: Going down the continental slope, where does the seafloor start to level out again?

options.label: At its base, where the rise begins

items.explain: At the base of the slope the angle suddenly decreases and the seafloor levels out; this zone is the continental rise.

items.prompt: How tall can the continental slope be, measured from the deep-ocean floor up to its top?
items.explain: The slope begins at the shelf break and can be 1–5 km above the deep-ocean floor.

items.prompt: Seafloor maps of the continental slope often show deep gashes running down it, sometimes reaching back onto the shelf. What are they?
items.explain: The slope often has submarine canyons, which cut deeply and can enlarge onto the continental shelf.

items.prompt: Which coast would you expect to have a narrow margin that drops steeply into a trench?

options.label: The East Coast of the United States
Any coast facing a mid-ocean ridge
The West Coast of South America
A coast far from any plate boundary

items.explain: The West Coast of South America is an active margin, and active margins are typically narrow with steep descents into trenches.

items.prompt: If you sliced across a submarine canyon on the continental slope, what cross-section shape would you most often see?

options.label: A wide U with a flat floor
A low mound rising above the slope

items.explain: These canyons are often V-shaped, with near-vertical sides.
